title: Polyphonic Escort Routing with Soft Anchoring and Capacity Currency
creator: Anika Bose
description: Design and implement a routing policy that balances latency affinity, capacity budgets, and graceful multi-region failover using a tokenized cross-region budget ('capacity currency') and soft-anchoring semantics for geo pinning. The aim is to reduce cross-region tail latency spikes during localized congestion while preserving cache/KV affinity and minimizing customer-visible errors during overloads.
rationale: Current hard-pin geo routing causes large error rates or long tails during regional saturation because once a region hits capacity we either 1) aggressively fail or 2) abruptly rehome all traffic with cache misses. We need a middle ground that honors locality but permits controlled borrowing and staged unpinning with observable economics so SLOs and cost trade-offs are explicit.
proposed_design: 1) Escort flows: for each user affinity group we maintain a primary region and one or two escort regions. Normal traffic uses primary; when primary lat/queueing exceeds soft thresholds we begin steering a controlled fraction to escort region(s) using a probabilistic multiplexer. 2) Soft anchoring: affinity TTLs are reduced gradually when congestion persists; pinned requests prefer primary but accept escort if latency budget breached. 3) Capacity currency: each region exposes a borrowable token pool; routers spend tokens to route to an escort region. Token costs are dynamic: high-cost during critical SLO breaches to disincentivize cross-region borrowing. 4) Quantile slack: use p50/p95/p99-informed thresholds to decide whether to initiate escorting vs local shed. 5) Circuit breakers: region-level circuits trip on error-rate and sustained queue-depth; when tripped, currency cost spikes and escorting increases or sheds to fallback models. 6) KV-cache hints: for requests likely to hit cold KV cache, prefer escort only if cache warmup heuristics predict acceptable cold-start penalty. 7) Telemetry tagging: every routed request gets routing_reason, token_spent, escort_fraction, origin_region, dest_region tags for downstream SLO attribution.
implementation_notes: - Router: extend dispatcher to support probabilistic escorting and token accounting. - Token service: lightweight distributed counter with per-region ledger and TTL-based replenishment. - Policy config: new policy type 'polyphonic_escort' with fields: primary_weight, escort_weights, slack_quantiles, token_cost_curve, unpin_grace_ms. - Backwards compatibility: default to existing geo-pin behavior if policy disabled. - Performance: routing decision must be sub-100us in hot path; token check should be cached locally with lease-based refreshes. - Failure modes: token service outage must degrade to safe defaults (no borrow; stricter shedding).
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: feature-flag candidate in us-west1 for internal traffic only (2 weeks). 2) Observability: enable detailed traces and metrics for canary routes to our dev dashboard. 3) Gradual ramp: expand to 10% of production traffic and monitor latency/error SLOs. 4) Emergency kill: single flag to revert to hard-pin routing. 5) Post-mortem and tuning: after 1 week stable, tune token_cost_curve and slack_quantiles. 6) GA: enable for selected customers as opt-in, then default after four cycles of telemetry-backed improvements.
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics: escort_rate_by_region, tokens_spent_per_min, region_borrow_ratio, p99_tail_by_region_with_escort, cache_miss_penalty_estimate. Alerts: - p99 increase >20% for 10m after escort enable (SEV-M) - tokens_spent spikes > 5x baseline (Ops) - region borrow ratio > 0.3 for >15m (SRE) - token service unavailability (P0). Dashboards: per-customer breakdown, routing_reason heatmap, token ledger view.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token accounting and probabilistic multiplexer; integration tests simulating region overloads and token exhaustion; perf benchmark to ensure <100us decision budget; chaos tests: token service outage, delayed replenishment, circuit-breaker flapping. Run smoke test against staging multi-region cluster with synthetic traffic shapes (steady-state, burst, sustained overload).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Router decision latency median <80us and 99th <120us under 95th percentile load. 2) In controlled overload tests, escorting reduces global p99 by >=10% vs forced local shedding while not increasing p50 by >5%. 3) Token accounting shows correct debits/credits in 99% of sampled requests. 4) No customer-visible error-rate regression >0.5% for opt-in customers during 72-hour ramp. 5) Telemetry tags present on 100% of routed requests. 6) Rollback path validated and exercised in canary.
